basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, microcephaly and cerebral atrophy; abnormal visual evoked potentials do not establish direct ocular damage.
Severe prenatal/postnatal growth restriction with skeletal abnormalities defines the phenotype; developmental delay occurs in 25%; no established endocrine gland dysfunction.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; skeletal muscle atrophy and esotropia each occur in 1/1 reported patient, with limited frequency evidence.
Defining triad of hypomyelination, dental abnormalities and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; myopia affects 80-99%.
Inherited Alzheimer disease causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Adult-onset cerebral white-matter disease with cognitive impairment; hypertensive retinopathy is a separate disease, and hypertension occurs in only 1/5.
Lymphoid malignancy arising in the thymus; hematologic lineage and lymphoma mechanism apply. Thymic location alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Focal inflammation of the choroid and retina, typically infectious or immune-mediated; no common extraocular injury is established.
Cerebral lysosomal lipid storage with dementia defines this umbrella; additional organ injury varies substantially between subtypes.
Inherited calcium-homeostasis disorder; renal insufficiency, stones and peptic ulcers are occasional (5-29%); other structural complications lack qualifying frequencies.
Inherited red-cell production failure causing Diamond-Blackfan anemia; no common direct extrahematologic injury is established.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with profound disability and movement abnormalities; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic, and sleep apnea is separately coded.
Telomere-related disorder defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or hypocellular bone marrow failure.
Neoplasm occupies the epicardium, a cardiac/pericardial structure.
Inherited bile-acid synthesis defects; cholestatic liver disease characterizes 7/9 described forms. Neurologic disease varies by subtype; malabsorption need not damage the gut.
Carcinoma originates in the nasal cavity/paranasal sinuses, included in the pulmonary axis; adjacent invasion is not established as common.
Umbrella of inherited sulfur amino-acid and methionine metabolism defects; neurologic, vascular and ocular injury is subtype-dependent.
Adrenal hypoplasia causes primary adrenal insufficiency, often with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; pigmentation and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish organ damage.
Umbrella for disorders located in the esophagus; infectious, immune and neoplastic mechanisms vary across subtypes.
Neoplasm originates in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; uterine smooth muscle is not locomotor skeletal muscle.
Congenital multivalvular dysplasia with frequent regurgitation and prolapse; musculoskeletal and ocular abnormalities are below 30%.
Renal ciliopathy with fibrosis and kidney failure; hepatobiliary structural involvement includes intrahepatic bile-duct dilation in 6/6 and hepatic cysts in 1/2.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection directly affects bones or joints; pulmonary disease is not required or established in most skeletal cases.
Adrenal disorder with severe intellectual disability and cutis laxa; skeletal deformities affect 80-99%; bladder diverticula (80-99%) omitted by four-axis cap.
Blood/marrow myelomonocytic neoplasm; liver infiltration in most, skin infiltration ~30-50%, pulmonary infiltration ~30-50%; splenic involvement shares the blood axis.
